label: Side is retreating
summary: Whether this side of a combat is the defeated one.
details: The game's description says "defeated"; the name says "retreating". The game does not say how the two relate. It works on a combat side. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Commands an army
summary: Whether the character is commanding an army.
details: Write `yes` to require a commander, `no` to require someone who does not command an army. Vanilla uses both about equally.

label: Travel is completed
summary: Whether a travel plan has finished, which means the traveller has arrived at the final destination.
details: It works on a travel plan. The game's note says a plan counts as completed when it ends by arriving at the final destination.

label: Is concubine
summary: Whether the character is a concubine.
details: Write `yes` to require a concubine, `no` to require someone who is not one.

label: Concubine of
summary: Whether the character is a concubine of the given character.
details: The checked character is the concubine, the character you write after the equals sign is the one they belong to. Vanilla writes a saved scope, `root` or a function parameter there.

label: In a confederation
summary: Whether the character is a member of a confederation.
details: Write `yes` to require a member, `no` to require someone outside any confederation.

label: County connected to
summary: Whether the county is connected to another county; the game says the check is based on the top liege.
details: The title it runs on is a county. `max_naval_distance` limits how far a sea link may reach, and `allow_one_county_land_gap = yes` lets one county in between be skipped. The game's usage example shows these two options; the vanilla uses seen here only write `target`, so the units of the distance and the exact effect of the gap are not stated.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The other county to check the connection to.
fields.values: a county title, usually a saved scope or a link

fields.name: max_naval_distance
fields.text: How far over water the connection may reach.

fields.name: allow_one_county_land_gap
fields.text: Whether a single county without a link may lie in between.

label: Consort of
summary: Whether the character is a spouse or a concubine of the given character.
details: The checked character is the consort, the character after the equals sign is their partner. It is the broad version: it covers both marriage and concubinage.

label: Is contact of
summary: Whether the checked character is a contact of the given character.
details: The game's description is unclear: it speaks of being the "employer of laamp", and its example is `scope:actor = { is_contact_of = SCOPE_CHARACTER }`. Vanilla writes `scope:actor`, `root` or `scope:laamp` after the equals sign. What kind of contact this is the game does not say here.

label: Is contested
summary: Whether the title is contested in any war.
details: It works on a landed title (a title that has land). `yes` means some war is being fought over it.

label: Council task is valid
summary: Whether the task of this councillor is still valid.
details: It runs on the councillor. You give the task type and, for tasks that need a target, the target. Vanilla only uses it with the find-secrets task.

fields.name: task_type
fields.text: The council position type whose task is checked.

fields.name: target
fields.text: The target of the task, for tasks that have one.
fields.values: a character, usually a saved scope or a link

label: Is councillor
summary: Whether the character is a councillor.
details: It does not say whose council. Use `is_councillor_of` to check a specific ruler. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Councillor of
summary: Whether the character is a councillor of the given ruler.
details: The checked character is the councillor, the character after the equals sign is the ruler whose council they sit on.

label: Is county capital
summary: Whether the province is the capital province of its county.
details: It works on a province. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Employs in court position
summary: Whether the checked character holds the given court position at the court of the given character.
details: The checked character is the employee. `who` is the one who employs them.

fields.name: court_position
fields.text: The court position the character holds.

fields.name: who
fields.text: The employer: the ruler at whose court they hold the position.
fields.values: a character, usually a saved scope, `root` or a link

label: Is courtier
summary: Whether the character is a courtier.
details: It does not say at whose court. Use `is_courtier_of` to check a specific ruler. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Courtier of
summary: Whether the character is a courtier at the court of the given character.
details: The checked character is the courtier, the character after the equals sign is the ruler. It is used very often in vanilla, mostly with `root`.

label: Cousin of
summary: Whether the character is a cousin of the given character.

label: Contract is criminal
summary: Whether the type of this contract is of a criminal nature.
details: It works on a task contract, not on a character. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Secret is criminal for
summary: Whether a secret counts as a crime for the given character.
details: It works on a secret. The character after the equals sign is the participant it is checked for. Vanilla often writes `secret_owner` there.

label: Culture is involved
summary: Whether the given culture takes part in the struggle.
details: It works on a struggle. The culture is written after the equals sign, e.g. `culture:english`.

label: Phase is running
summary: Whether the current phase of the activity is in its active state.
details: `no` means the phase is in its passive state instead. It works on an activity.

label: De facto liege or above
summary: Whether the title is the de facto liege of the target title, or a title above it.
details: De facto means by who actually holds the titles now, not by the map's borders. The checked title is the higher one, the title after the equals sign is the lower one. Compare `is_de_jure_liege_or_above_target`.

label: De jure liege or above
summary: Whether the title is the de jure liege of the target title, or a title above it.
details: De jure means by the map's fixed borders (which kingdom a county belongs to), not by who holds what now. The checked title is the higher one, the title after the equals sign is the lower one. Vanilla often writes `prev` there.

label: Faith is dead
summary: Whether the faith is dead, meaning no county and no character practises it any more.
details: The game's description is cut off after naming those two conditions, so there may be a further condition it does not show. Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Decision on cooldown
summary: Whether the given decision is on cooldown for the character.
details: The decision is written after the equals sign by its key. Vanilla uses it only a few times.

label: Defender is
summary: Whether the given character is in the war as a defender.
details: It runs on the war; the character after the equals sign is the one checked. Compare `is_defender_in_war`, which runs on the character.

label: Defender in war
summary: Whether the character is in the given war as a defender.
details: It runs on the character; the war is written after the equals sign. Compare `is_defender`, which runs on the war.

label: Is designated diarch
summary: Whether the character was designated as diarch by their liege.
details: It asks about the designation by the liege. For being an active diarch, see `is_diarch`. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Is diarch
summary: Whether the character is currently an active diarch of anyone.
details: It does not say of whom. Use `is_diarch_of_target` for a specific ruler. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Diarch of
summary: Whether the character is currently an active diarch of the given character.
details: The checked character is the diarch, the character after the equals sign is the ruler they are diarch of. Vanilla often writes `liege` or `top_liege` there.

label: Is diarchy successor
summary: Whether the character is next in the line of succession for the diarchy.
details: Vanilla only writes `yes`.

label: Directed at a target
summary: Whether the great holy war is a directed one.
details: The game gives no further description of a directed holy war. It works on a great holy war (GHW). The app's own label says "directed at a target".

label: Is divergent culture
summary: Whether the culture was created by diverging from a single parent culture.
details: `no` requires a culture that did not come about this way. Vanilla uses both values.

label: Kind of domicile
summary: Whether the domicile is of the given type.
details: The type is written after the equals sign by its key. Vanilla names types like `estate`, `yurt`, `camp` and `japanese_manor`.

label: Is dominant family
summary: Whether the house is considered a dominant family.
details: It works on a dynasty house. The game does not explain here what makes a house dominant.

label: Employer of
summary: Whether the given character is a courtier of the checked character.
details: The direction is the reverse of `is_courtier_of`: here the checked character is the ruler, the one after the equals sign is the courtier.

label: Equipped
summary: Whether the artifact is currently equipped in its owner's inventory.
details: It works on an artifact. Write `yes` or `no`.

label: Event regiment
summary: Whether a men-at-arms regiment is part of the event troops.
details: It works on a regiment. The game documents nothing more, and vanilla does not use it.

label: Extended family of
summary: Whether the character is extended family of the given character.
details: Extended family means cousins, uncles, aunts, nephews and nieces, according to the game.
